accepted.question_text: Consider the single-input time-optimal control system qdot = f(q) + u g(q) with |u| ≤ 1 on a 3-dimensional smooth manifold M, where f and g are a generic smooth pair of vector fields. Must every time-optimal trajectory for this generic 3-dimensional problem be piecewise smooth, meaning that the trajectory has only finitely many switching points and is smooth between them?

evidence.quote: A. (f, g) is a generic pair of vector fields. Optimal trajectories cannot be all smooth; are they piecewise smooth?
The question is open for n = 3.

accepted.question_text: For the same generic single-input time-optimal control problem qdot = f(q) + u g(q) with |u| ≤ 1 on a 3-dimensional manifold, let sw(q) denote the smallest local uniform bound on the number of switching points of sufficiently short time-optimal trajectories near q, with sw(q) = ∞ if arbitrarily close optimal trajectories can have infinitely many switching points. Is sw(q) finite for every point q in M?

evidence.quote: We do not know if sw(q) < ∞ for any q ∈ M.

accepted.question_text: For a generic smooth pair of vector fields f and g in the single-input time-optimal system qdot = f(q) + u g(q), |u| ≤ 1, on a 3-dimensional manifold, must each individual time-optimal trajectory have only finitely many switching points, even if no uniform bound over nearby trajectories is assumed?

evidence.quote: We also do not know if a weaker property, the finiteness of the number of switching points for any individual time-optimal trajectory is valid.

accepted.question_text: Let M be a real analytic manifold and let f and g be real analytic vector fields in the time-optimal control system qdot = f(q) + u g(q), |u| ≤ 1. If two points are connected by some time-optimal trajectory, is there always a time-optimal trajectory joining the same endpoints whose set of switching points is at most countable?

evidence.quote: Main open question here is as follows: Given two points connected by a time-optimal trajectory, can we connect them by a time-optimal trajectory with no more than a countable number of switching points?

accepted.question_text: In the same real analytic time-optimal control setting, can one always avoid time-optimal trajectories whose switching points occupy a set of positive measure? Equivalently, whenever two points can be joined by a time-optimal trajectory, must there exist such a trajectory whose switching set has measure zero?

evidence.quote: We do not know if we can avoid a positive measure set of switching points.

accepted.question_text: Let Δ ⊂ TM be a bracket-generating distribution defining a sub-Riemannian structure on a manifold M, and let γ0, γ1 : [0,1] → M be smooth admissible paths with the same starting point q0 and linearly independent initial velocities at q0. Must there always exist an admissible path from γ0(1) to γ1(1) whose length is strictly less than the length of the broken path obtained by concatenating γ0 and γ1?

evidence.quote: Does there exist an admissible path connecting γ0(1) with γ1(1) that is strictly shorter than the concatenation of the curves γ0 and γ1?

Any improvement of the estimates for m and n would be very interesting. We still know very little about sub-Riemannian structures with big m and it may happen that the answer is negative for some m and n.

accepted.question_text: For a sub-Riemannian structure on a manifold M and a fixed starting point q0, consider the endpoint map from the Hilbert manifold of H1 admissible paths starting at q0 to M, sending each path γ to γ(1). Must this endpoint map always have at least one regular value, or can the singular curves issuing from q0 fill the entire manifold M?

evidence.quote: The endpoint maps have plenty of regular points but we do not know if they always have regular values.
We can reformulate the question as follows: is it possible that starting from q0 singular curves fill the whole manifold M?

accepted.question_text: For the same endpoint-map setting in sub-Riemannian geometry, can length-minimizing singular curves issuing from a fixed point q0 fill a subset of M of positive measure, or is their image always measure-theoretically small?

evidence.quote: An important open question: can they fill a positive measure subset of M?

accepted.question_text: For a generic sub-Riemannian metric on a rank-2 Martinet distribution in ℝ3, where points of the Martinet surface lie on optimal singular curves, what is the C1 classification of the germs of small sub-Riemannian spheres at points where the sphere meets an optimal singular curve? In other words, how do these sphere singularities look up to local C1 diffeomorphism in the generic Martinet case?

evidence.quote: An important open question is to find a C1-classification of the germs of spheres at the points of optimal singular curves for generic metrics.

accepted.question_text: For the Engel distribution, that is, a rank-2 distribution in ℝ4 with n3(q) = 3 and n4(q) = 4, what is the C1 classification of the germs of sub-Riemannian spheres at points lying on the optimal singular curve through the point? Equivalently, how should one classify these 3-dimensional hypersurface singularities in ℝ4 up to local C1 diffeomorphism?

evidence.quote: The next step is the Engel distribution, i. e. a rank 2 distribution in R4 such that n3(q) = 3, n4(q) = 4. There is exactly one singular curve through any point and small segments of singular curves are optimal. We repeat our question for this case; the spheres are now 3-dimensional hypersurfaces in R4.
Hence the solution of the problem in the 4-dimensional Engel case is a very important step in the unfolding of the sphere for any n ≥ 4.

accepted.question_text: Let q0 ∈ ℝ2 and let f0, f1 be smooth vector fields defined near q0 such that f0(q0) ∧ f1(q0) = 0, n2(q0) = 1, and n3(q0) = 2. For the almost-Riemannian control system qdot = u0 f0(q) + u1 f1(q) with unit-speed constraint, what is the C1 classification of the germs of the distance function Sq0 for generic pairs (f0, f1) satisfying these conditions?

evidence.quote: The question is to find a C1-classification of the germs of distance functions Sq0 for generic pairs of vector fields f0, f1 among the pairs that satisfy conditions n2(q0) = 1, n3(q0) = 2.

accepted.question_text: Let Δ ⊂ TM be a smooth vector distribution on a manifold M. Suppose Δ is singular transitive, meaning that any two points of M can be joined by a concatenation of singular curves of Δ. Does this singular transitivity force the full symmetry group of Δ—the diffeomorphisms Φ with Φ_*Δ = Δ—to be a finite-dimensional Lie group?

evidence.quote: A natural open question is as follows: Is it true that singular transitivity of the distribution implies that its symmetry group is a finite dimensional Lie group?

accepted.question_text: For rank-2 distributions that are not singular transitive, is the symmetry group always infinite-dimensional? The question asks whether the finite-dimensionality phenomenon might fail completely outside the singular-transitive case for rank-2 distributions.

evidence.quote: We can even expect that any not singular transitive rank 2 distribution has an infinite dimensional symmetry group.

accepted.question_text: For each n > 3, determine the smallest integer μ(n) such that any convex plane curve run μ(n) times admits arbitrarily small perturbations as a nondegenerate closed curve in ℝn, and decide whether every regular closed curve in ℝn has Frenet-frame length strictly greater than μ(n) times the length of the standard closed geodesic SO(2) ⊂ O(n).

evidence.quote: An important open problem is to find µ(n) for n > 3 and to check if the length of the Frenet frame of any regular curve in Rn is greater than the length of SO(2) ⊂ O(n) multiplied by µ(n).

accepted.question_text: Consider the incompressible Navier–Stokes equation on the torus with forcing restricted to a control space E. If D is an open subset of the torus, does there exist a finite-dimensional subspace E of the closure of {u ∈ V : supp u ⊂ D} that is independent of the viscosity ν and still makes the system approximately controllable, or controllable in finite-dimensional projections, by localized degenerate forcing?

evidence.quote: Now an important open question: is the system approximately controllable and (or) controllable in the finite dimensional projections by a localized degenerate forcing when E is a finite dimensional subspace of the space {u ∈ V : supp u ⊂ D}¯ ?
The question is about existence and effective construction of such a space E that does not depend on the viscosity ν.

accepted.question_text: For a fixed compact 3-dimensional contact manifold with a chosen contact distribution, can one define a natural averaging or heat-type evolution on the space of sub-Riemannian metrics that converges, possibly after suitable rescaling, to a nonzero generalized metric preserved by the Reeb field, even when no smooth Reeb-invariant metric exists? This includes understanding whether the discrete averaging scheme or the continuous equation ∂h/∂t = c{uh,{uh,h}} can produce meaningful limiting Hamiltonians with controlled singularities.

evidence.quote: To conclude, I would like to discuss one more problem; it is less precise than already stated questions but, to my taste, is nice and fascinating. The problem concerns contact 3-dimensional manifolds and is inspired by the Ricci flow story.
There is a good chance to arrive to a nonzero limiting Hamiltonian h∞ by a clever choice of the sequences of positive functions εn, cn.
A continuous time analogue of the introduced dynamics is a "heat along the Reeb field" equation ∂h/∂t = c{uh, {uh, h}} in the space of sub-Riemannian metrics on the given contact distribution.
